chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Rifa'ah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the woman whose husband dies while he is absent, when should she observe her waiting period? He said: 'The day the news reaches her.' And he mentioned that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'One of you women used to remain for a year when her husband died and he was absent, then she would cast her desires behind her back.'
ai.seo_question: When does the waiting period begin for a widow if her husband dies while he is absent?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies that the waiting period (iddah) for a widow whose husband dies while absent begins upon the actual receipt of news, rather than a fixed duration from the date of death. It references a prophetic precedent where women observed a full year of mourning in such cases, highlighting the transition from extended customary mourning to the standardized four months and ten days prescribed in Islamic law.
